channel.title: Ting · A Personal Journal
channel.description: Ting's personal journal at the crossing of control research, engineering and design.

item.title: Teaching Neurons to Fire: Surrogate Gradients and Spiking Networks in EEG Decoding
item.description: Spikes are 0 or 1; gradients are continuous — once surrogate gradients bridge that gap, spiking networks overtake their ANN prototypes on EEG decoding.

item.title: Booking the Settling Time with Delayed Feedback: Notes on Deng et al. (2024)
item.description: Close reading of Deng et al., IEEE TAC 2024: a nonsingular predefined-time terminal sliding mode control built on artificial-delay sliding surfaces, with notes on relevance to CAV control.

item.title: In the Beginning: Why I'm Starting a Personal Journal
item.description: Who I am, what the five sections hold, and why I'm building this site.

item.title: Why 4-bit Doesn't Lose Accuracy: Quantization-Aware Training and Device Non-idealities
item.description: Stuff a neural network into analog hardware and the weights drop to 4 bits with noise always lurking — QAT's answer: don't face the hardware after training ends; live inside it during training.

item.title: Slicing Time into 72 ps: The Quantized-Delay Method and Coarse-Fine Counting in TDCs
item.description: What do you do when a stopwatch's ticks are too coarse? Turn the carry chain into a delay ruler ticked cell by cell, then pair coarse and fine counting to stretch the range to milliseconds — that is the whole secret of TDCs on FPGAs.

item.title: Two 5 GHz Halves Make One 10 GHz Whole: Bandwidth Interleaving and the Overlap-Band Notch
item.description: One ADC can't capture 10 GHz, so use two, each capturing half, then stitch — the hard part is not the split but the notch tens of dB deep at the seam: where it comes from and how to remove it.
